knowledge_point.title: Identifying Parallel Lines Given in Standard Form

question.:question/problem: Which of the following lines is parallel to $-5x+y=-5$?
question.:question/worked-solution:
For two distinct nonvertical lines to be parallel, they must have the same slope.

To find the slope of $-5x+y=-5$, convert to slope-intercept form:

$$
\begin{aligned}
-5x+y &= -5 \\
y &= 5x-5 \\
y &= 5x-5
\end{aligned}
$$

The slope is the coefficient of $x$, so the required slope is $5$.

Only $y=5x-4$ has slope $5$.

The line $y=5x-4$ has slope $5$ and $y$-intercept $-4$, different from $-5$. Therefore, it is a distinct parallel line.

$$
y=5x-4
$$

question.:question/problem: Which of the following is a distinct line parallel to $2x+3y=-9$?
question.:question/worked-solution:
For two distinct nonvertical lines to be parallel, they must have the same slope.

To find the slope of $2x+3y=-9$, convert to slope-intercept form:

$$
\begin{aligned}
2x+3y &= -9 \\
3y &= -2x-9 \\
y &= -\frac{2}{3}x-3
\end{aligned}
$$

The slope is the coefficient of $x$, so the required slope is $-\frac{2}{3}$.

Rewrite the choices in slope-intercept form:

$$
\begin{aligned}
-6x-9y=9 &\quad\Longrightarrow\quad y=-\frac{2}{3}x-1 \\
-10x+2y=-4 &\quad\Longrightarrow\quad y=5x-2 \\
18x+3y=0 &\quad\Longrightarrow\quad y=-6x \\
15x-3y=-3 &\quad\Longrightarrow\quad y=5x+1 \\
-2x-3y=9 &\quad\Longrightarrow\quad y=-\frac{2}{3}x-3
\end{aligned}
$$

The line $-2x-3y=9$ has both the same slope $-\frac{2}{3}$ and the same $y$-intercept $-3$ as the given line. It is the same line, so it is not a distinct parallel line.

The line $-6x-9y=9$ has slope $-\frac{2}{3}$ and $y$-intercept $-1$, different from $-3$. Therefore, it is a distinct parallel line.

$$
-6x-9y=9
$$
